diag.vram_not_applicable:
THIS IS NOT APPLIED FROM HERE YET. Touching the cmdline means touching the
  bootloader — the only change in this app that can leave a machine unable to
  boot. It only ships with an ADDITIONAL GRUB entry (the original untouched),
  a backup, and one parameter at a time. See ADR-0011 §5.
gpu.amd_no_gtt: the GPU is AMD, but the driver did not expose GTT under /sys — without the current value there is no honest ceiling to suggest
gpu.intel_firmware: on Intel the integrated GPU's memory is fixed by FIRMWARE (DVMT), in the UEFI setup — Linux does not change it at runtime. To change it, it is in the board's setup, not here
gpu.nvidia_own_vram: a discrete NVIDIA GPU uses its own VRAM, not system RAM through GTT — there is nothing to cap here
gpu.unknown_vendor: could not identify the GPU vendor under /sys/class/drm — I will not suggest a kernel parameter blindly
limits.after_apply:
To take effect now:
    systemctl --user daemon-reload

The ceilings apply to whatever is STARTED inside the slice. E.g.:
    systemd-run --user --slice=dev-build.slice --scope cargo build

Undo everything with: optimizer limits --revert
limits.cpu_none: cpu    : no ceiling (a build slowed by a quota defeats the purpose)
limits.dry_run:
Nothing was changed. To apply:
    optimizer limits --apply
And to undo, at any time:
    optimizer limits --revert
limits.io: io     : weight {weight} (100 is the default; lower yields to the interactive)
limits.memory: memory : throttles at {high} MiB, kills at {max} MiB
limits.no_cgroups: cgroups v2 is not mounted — without it systemd ignores the limits silently, and writing the files would give the impression that something was done
limits.nothing_to_revert: nothing to revert (no box from this tool was applied).
limits.opposites: `--apply` and `--revert` are opposites — ask for one at a time
limits.reload_systemd:
Reload the user systemd for it to take effect now:
    systemctl --user daemon-reload

NOTHING TO SUGGEST
  The allowlisted services either are not enabled here, or cost nothing
  measurable in this boot. Touching the system for zero gain is the opposite
  of optimising.
services.we_do_not_touch:
This tool does NOT disable anything by itself. Disabling a service is where machines
break, and the cause ends up far from the symptom — read what you lose, decide item by
item, and run the command yourself.
svc.appstream.does: refreshes the application store's metadata cache
svc.appstream.lose: the application store may show an outdated catalogue until you refresh it by hand
svc.appstream.why: it is for the graphical software storefront. Whoever installs with `zypper`/`apt` in the terminal never reads that cache
svc.nm_wait.does: holds the boot until the network is up
svc.nm_wait.lose: if you have an NFS/SMB mount in /etc/fstab, or a service that requires the network at boot, it may fail on the first attempt
svc.nm_wait.why: on a desktop nothing needs the network BEFORE login — what needs it is a server with a network mount, or a service that starts alongside. The desktop connects in the background and the login does not wait
